errorCodes.meaning: The agent holds no update key for this DID.
The DID's latest entry no longer matches `expectedVersionId` — someone else updated it since the caller read it. The caller SHOULD re-read and re-apply its edits.
The document is not a valid DID document for this subject (for example, its `id` does not match `did`).
`scidAlsoKnownAs` is `false`, or `document` omits the alias, for an identity the agent presents in the did:scid form. That form exists only while the did:webvh document lists it (VTI-KEY-166).

The request would publish an entry identical in document and parameters to the latest one — for example `scidAlsoKnownAs: true` for a log that already lists the alias. Nothing is published, and the update key is not rotated.

Response.description: The published entry. camelCase per the framework convention — note the counts are the state AFTER the update, including the rotation the caller did not ask for.

newLogEntry.description: The appended log entry, as JSON text.

newVersionId.description: versionId of the entry just appended. A caller intending a further edit SHOULD pass this back as the next request's `expectedVersionId`.

preRotationKeyCount.description: Pre-rotation commitments published by this entry.

scidAlsoKnownAs.description: Whether the published document lists `scidDidUrl` in `alsoKnownAs`. A 1.1 consumer MUST report it; it is optional in the schema only because 1.1 extends 1.0.

scidDidUrl.description: The `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=<source>` DID URL of the log at its current location — the did:scid DID with the locator a recipient needs to resolve it. Reported whether or not it is listed. A 1.1 consumer MUST report it; it is optional in the schema only because 1.1 extends 1.0.

serverless.description: True when the agent holds the log itself and no hosting server was published to — the operator must fetch and redeploy `did.jsonl`.

updateKeysCount.description: Update keys authorized AFTER this entry. Where `document` was supplied these are new keys — the previous ones no longer authorize anything.

Response.title: WebVH DID Update — response payload

schema.description: Ask a Verifiable Trust Agent to publish a new entry in a did:webvh log it holds the update key for. The agent decides whether to do so; the caller proposes.

did.description: The did:webvh being updated. The agent MUST verify it speaks for this subject.

document.description: The new DID document. Omit to leave it unchanged. Supplying this ROTATES the DID's update key and refreshes its pre-rotation commitments, as a parallel consequence of the change — a consequence not visible anywhere in this payload, because it lives in the executing handler's semantics. A consent surface MUST therefore render effects the executor computed, and MUST NOT derive them from this document.

expectedVersionId.description: Optimistic-concurrency precondition: the versionId the caller based this edit on. The agent MUST refuse the update if the DID's latest entry no longer matches. Without it a `get -> edit -> save` cycle silently overwrites a concurrent edit with a chain that is structurally valid, verifies perfectly, and is based on a stale read. Where a human approves the update the window is minutes wide, so this is a routine race rather than an exotic one. OPTIONAL because a scripted caller with no concurrent writers has nothing to protect against; not optional for anything a person looked at.

preRotationCount.description: Number of pre-rotation commitments to publish. Omit to keep the current count; `0` disables pre-rotation going forward.

scidAlsoKnownAs.description: Whether the published document lists this log's `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=<source>` DID URL in `alsoKnownAs`, linking the did:webvh and did:scid forms as one subject (VTI-KEY-164). `true` adds it, for the log's current location, after the entries the document already has; `false` removes every did:scid entry naming this log's SCID. Applied to `document` when one is supplied, otherwise to the current document. Omit to leave `alsoKnownAs` as `document` (or the current document) has it. The agent derives the DID URL itself — the caller never writes it. Changing it publishes an entry, and so ROTATES the update key exactly as supplying `document` does.

ttl.description: New TTL in seconds. Omit to keep the current value.

watchers.description: New watcher URLs. Omit to keep the current set; an empty array removes them.

witnesses.description: New witness configuration. Omit to keep the current one.
